answer: A marketplace can require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, nontransferable credential earned through verified work, then slash that bond when independent audits catch duplicate identities coordinating to claim rewards. Auditors compare signed task histories and payment flows, so merely changing names or keys does not reset reputation. The attacker must fund and maintain many histories, while risking every bond; scaling a sybil fleet therefore becomes costly. At dawn, a wharf operator might audit ridge deliveries before releasing payment.
